quote: The dipping dashi for Hiroshima tsukemen is built on chashu and a savory soy-based sauce, which conventionally contains wheat; no gluten-free preparation is documented.
found: Gnavi says only 「天然利尻昆布とチャーシューで取ったダシはあっさりした味わいで、ゆでた野菜が甘みを添えています」 — zero occurrences of 醤油 on the whole page. The soy-sauce evidence is on the shop's own Tabelog page: 「つけダレの辛味はもとよりキレのある醤油ベースの味わいと酸味にマッチ」 and 「魚介系と野菜の出汁に醤油とチャーシュー煮汁のコクが足されている」.
method: 1 plain fetch (gnavi) + 1 mobile-UA fetch (tabelog detail page)
note: Claim is TRUE but cited to the wrong page — Gnavi never mentions soy sauce. Re-cite to the Tabelog detail page, where two independent reviewers describe the tare as 醤油ベース. Neither page contains 小麦/グルテン/アレル, so 'no gluten-free preparation documented' stands by silence.

quote: The signature broth is made with pork chashu, so the kitchen handles animal products throughout the core dish.
found: 「広島つけ麺で知られる「冷麺かず」では、天然利尻昆布とチャーシューで取ったダシはあっさりした味わい」
note: Supported. Tabelog reviews corroborate and add detail — a regular was told the cold soup is not 鶏ガラ/豚骨 but 昆布や鰹節類 plus chashu simmering liquid; still fish + pork, so vegan: no is correct, and the fish-stock component is worth adding to vegan_detail.

quote: Menu includes breaded/deep-fried oysters (kaki fry) and other fried items shared with wheat-based cooking; no dedicated gluten-free fryer or protocol is documented.
found: 「かきフライ　または　天ぷら（3個）」 and 「生がき・焼きがき・かきフライ・・・」; a 2018 review adds 「人気の穴子の天ぷらも食べることができました」. Page contains no アレルギー/グルテン/小麦 text of any kind.
note: Supported. Kaki-fry and tempura are both on the official Hot Pepper menu; the no-GF-protocol half is true by silence (no allergen section on the listing).

quote: Japanese-style dishes use standard soy sauce, which contains wheat; no wheat-free seasoning is mentioned.
found: The word 醤油 appears zero times on the page. The seasonings it does document point the other way: 「レモンと藻塩だけでお召し上がりいただきます」 (kaki fry), 「地穴子を白焼きにして、藻塩と山葵でいただきます」, 「オリーブオイルをかけて…」 (tako grill), 「素材の味を引き立たせるため、シンプルな調理法にてご提供」.
method: 1 plain fetch + in-page keyword scan for 醤油/しょうゆ/たまり
note: Unsupported, and mildly wrong in direction: the cited page's own copy stresses salt-and-lemon / moshio-and-wasabi / olive-oil finishing on the headline oyster, anago and octopus dishes. The soy-sauce line is an unevidenced genre assumption. Reword as an assumption or drop it; the wheat hazard here is the fry/tempura batter and the Italian pasta and bread, which are documented.

quote: The kitchen centers on seafood (oysters, anago, octopus, sashimi) and meat; vegetable dishes would share equipment and fish/dashi-based seasonings.
found: Page strapline 「かき・たこ・穴子・広島地酒・ワイン・個室・ジビエ・Tボーンステーキ・ランチ」 plus menu items 焼きがき、たこ足のグリル、倉吉牛Tボーンステーキ、鹿もも肉のグリル、ねぎトロ、音戸ちりめんのカリカリサラダ.
note: Supported for the menu-composition half (even the salad is topped with dried whitebait). The 'shared equipment and fish/dashi seasonings' half is inference, not on the page — fine as reasoning but should not read as documented fact.

quote: Dishes are seasoned with soy-sauce-based seasonings; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
found: 醤油 / タレ / 出汁 all return zero hits on the cited homepage, and zero again on https://irori-sasa.jp/lunch/ and https://irori-sasa.jp/takeout/. The official site describes only cooking methods (藁炙り焼き・原始焼き・薪焼き・炭火焼き) and 「瀬戸内の鮮魚、地元産のお野菜を中心に」 — never a seasoning.
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited page + 2 plain fetches of the site's only two menu subpages, keyword-scanned
note: Unsupported — pure genre assumption, no soy sauce mentioned anywhere on this operator's site. The real, documented wheat exposure is stronger and should replace it: every course lists 揚物, the fugu courses list 唐揚, and /lunch/ sells a 茶そば御膳 with 天ぷら (chasoba is wheat noodles). gf_confidence 'no' remains correct on that evidence.

quote: Cooking is centered on a shared hearth, kiln and charcoal grill used for fish, oysters and meat, so vegetable items would share fire and surfaces with animal proteins.
found: The homepage supports the hearth-and-fish half only: 「当店では「藁炙り焼き」「原始焼き」「薪焼き」「炭火焼き」の手法を使い分け」, 「囲炉裏のあるカウンターは…魚の焼ける音や香りが」, 「瀬戸内の鮮魚 旬の美味を厳選仕入れ」. Meat is documented one page over at /lunch/: 「旬魚とイベリコ豚ロース炭焼き」「和牛炭火焼き」「和牛とトマトのすき焼き」「牛ハラミ御膳」. Oysters appear on NEITHER page, nor on /takeout/ — 牡蠣/かき is zero hits site-wide.
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited page + 2 plain fetches of the sibling menu pages
note: Split citation: cite the homepage for the shared hearth and Setouchi fish, add https://irori-sasa.jp/lunch/ for the charcoal-grilled Iberico pork and wagyu. Then DELETE 'oysters' — it is unevidenced on this operator's whole site and also appears in the record's vegan_detail ('centers on seafood (oysters, Seto Inland Sea fish)'). Looks like a Hiroshima-genre assumption imported into a specific venue.

quote: Dishes are cooked on a shared teppan (griddle) where wheat-batter okonomiyaki and noodles are prepared, making cross-contact with gluten effectively unavoidable.
found: 「村長デラックス 1,925円 そば・生イカ・エビ・チーズ・ネギかけ・豚肉・玉子、ボリュームたっぷりのお好み焼き♪」, 「そば・もち・チーズ入り 1,408円」, menu sections 【てっぱん焼きとおつまみ】 and 【てっぱん あつあつメニュー】, and 「広々空間と大きい鉄板が魅力的な店内です★」 / 「1階はカウンターとテーブル席の30席。お気軽感と目の前で焼いてくれるのがいい！」.
note: Supported. Worth strengthening: the same shared griddle also turns out タコの天ぷら, じゃこ天 and 黒豚ギョーザ — three more wheat items — and the all-you-can-eat plan is okonomiyaki and negiyaki. Page carries no アレルギー/グルテン/小麦 text at all.

quote: Okonomiyaki is finished with okonomiyaki/Worcestershire-style sauce, which is wheat- and soy-based.
found: 「そば・もち・チーズ入り 1,408円 (税込) お好み焼きのソースとチーズのトロトロ感が相性抜群！女性人気ナンバー1♪」 — the only occurrence of ソース on the page, and 醤油 is zero.
method: 1 plain fetch + keyword scan for ソース/醤油/小麦
note: The shop page evidences THAT okonomiyaki sauce is used; it does not evidence what is in it — the wheat-and-soy composition is off-page product knowledge, and the field name (soy_sauce_wheat) overstates what the citation carries. Either reword to 'finished with okonomiyaki sauce' and keep this citation, or add a manufacturer allergen listing (Otafuku) for the wheat half. Not a safety error: the batter and soba noodles already make this a hard no.
